Subject: Model fit & prompt collection - follow-up

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier - it was helpful to see Redwood's latency and cost controls. A few quick recaps from our side and asks as we try to qualify model fit: 

- Our primary use case is support-response generation for our web app (short form, multi-turn).
- Constraints: PII redaction before storage, data residency in US only, and predictable 95th-pct latency under 600ms for single-turn responses.
- Quality: highest priority is preserving factual accuracy and avoiding hallucinations for billing-related queries.

As discussed, we'd like to share a first-pass set of customer prompts and edge cases so you can recommend model variants and a benchmark plan. I've attached a CSV with ~80 sample prompts (acme_prompt_samples.csv). Can you: 
1) Recommend 2-3 model variants we should evaluate (including quantized options).
2) Share any benchmark links or previous evals that map to support-style prompts.
3) Provide guidance on redaction expectations/formatting so we can strip PII client-side.

Also looping in Acme Legal (acme-legal@acme.com) to track the data residency question.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Smith
Head of Product, Acme Corp

Hi Jordan - great to meet you and thanks for sending the sample prompts. Quick responses inline and next steps: 

1) Recommended models:
   - Redwood-Chat-XL (hosted) - best balance for short multi-turn; strong safety mitigations.
   - Llama2-13B-q4f (quantized) - good cost/latency for Dedicated or Private deployments; we expect ~30-40% cost savings with modest quality trade-offs.
   - Falcon-Instruct-40B (if you need stronger instruction-following, higher cost/latency).

2) Benchmarks & evals:
   - We've uploaded a tailored benchmark run for support-style prompts here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-benchmarks
   - See attached quick summary (redwood_model_benchmarks.pdf) - includes latency percentiles and QA accuracy on a similar support dataset.

3) Prompt collection & redaction guidance:
   - Please use our prompt collection template (attached: prompt_collection_template.csv). Columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_intent, sensitive_fields_masked (yes/no), notes.
   - For PII: replace emails with <EMAIL_REDACTED>, phone numbers with <PHONE_REDACTED>, and account IDs with <ACCT_REDACTED>. Keep a mapping file locally if you need to re-link responses.
   - We recommend including expected outputs/examples for at least 30 edge-case prompts so our evals can compute regression rates.

Action items / next steps:
- Jordan: share the full prompt set using the template (can drop in the shared Drive link) - target by EOD next Tue (2026-05-18).
- Redwood (Rafael/Vivek): we'll run an initial model-fit eval on the 80 prompts and return recommendations + a quick benchmark report by 2026-05-20.

cc'ing Rafael (sales lead) to align on next steps and Vivek from infra to confirm redaction/ingestion constraints. Happy to hop on a 30m follow-up if useful - what does next Wed look like?

Best,

Jordan - appreciate the edge cases. Quick follow-ups from our side: 

- Example redactions (before -> after):
  1) "Hi John, can you confirm on john.doe@client.com?" -> "Hi John, can you confirm on <EMAIL_REDACTED>?"
  2) "Order 123-456-789 for +1 (555) 123-4567" -> "Order <ACCT_REDACTED> for <PHONE_REDACTED>"

- Yes - our eval pipeline supports masked placeholders and will compute intent/quality metrics against expected outputs. One caveat: if the prompt relies on the exact tokenization of IDs for retrieval matches, include a local mapping file (never shared) so you can re-link offline.

- Vivek: can you confirm whether we should run the initial eval on Hosted Redwood-Chat-XL or spin up a quick Dedicated job on Llama2-13B-q4f for more realistic latency numbers? Rafael, I put tentative slots on my calendar for Wed 2026-05-20 10:00-10:30 and Thu 2026-05-21 14:00-14:30 to review the benchmark results.
